i0: We use the **second conditional** for situations that are **imaginary** now or **unlikely** in the future: *If I **had** a car, I**'d drive** to work.* (I don't have a car.)
i1: The *if* clause uses a **past** form, but the meaning is **not past**. For real, possible situations, see [Zero and First Conditional](/blog/grammar/zero-and-first-conditional/). For the past, see [Third Conditional](/blog/grammar/third-conditional/).
sc-form-use.t: Form and use: if + past simple, would + verb
sc-form-use.s: **if + past simple, would + base verb** for an imaginary or unlikely situation: *If I won the lottery, I'd travel the world.*
sc-form-use.b0.h: if-clause (past simple) | main clause (would + base verb)
sc-form-use.b1: The past form in the *if* clause doesn't mean the past. It shows that the situation is **not real** or **not likely**: *If I **had** a dog…* = I don't have a dog.
sc-form-use.b2: The short form of *would* is ***'d***: *I**'d** go, she**'d** help.* The negative is ***wouldn't***.
sc-form-use.b3: Don't use *would* in the *if* clause: *If I **had** time…* Not *If I would have time…*
sc-form-use.w0: No would in the if clause.
sc-questions.s: Questions: **What would you do if** you lost your phone? Short answers: *Yes, I would. / No, I wouldn't.*
sc-questions.b0: To ask about an imaginary situation, use ***would*** + subject + base verb: ***What would** you **do** if you **lost** your passport?*
sc-questions.b1: The *if* clause can come first: ***If** you **could** live anywhere, **where would** you **live**?*
sc-questions.b2: Short answers use *would / wouldn't*: ***Would** you **help** me if I asked? ~ Yes, I **would**.*
sc-questions.b3: In speaking, *would you* often sounds like /wʊdʒu/. Don't drop it: *What **would you** do?* Not *What you would do?*
sc-questions.w1: No would in the if clause.
sc-vs-first.s: First = a **real** possibility (*If I win, I'll…*). Second = **imaginary or unlikely** (*If I won, I'd…*). The speaker chooses.
sc-vs-first.b0.0.0: *If it **rains** tomorrow, we**'ll stay** in.* (it may rain)
sc-vs-first.b0.0.1: *If it **rained** every day, I**'d move** to Spain.* (imaginary)
sc-vs-first.b0.1.0: *If I **get** the job, I**'ll buy** a car.* (I've had an interview)
sc-vs-first.b0.1.1: *If I **got** the job, I**'d buy** a car.* (it's unlikely)
sc-vs-first.b0.2.0: *If you **come** to Toronto, you**'ll love** it.*
sc-vs-first.b0.2.1: *If you **lived** in Toronto, you**'d love** it.*
sc-vs-first.b1: Sometimes both are possible. The choice shows **how likely** the speaker thinks the situation is: *If I **win** the match, I'll be so happy* (I think I can win). *If I **won** the match, I'd be so happy* (I probably won't).
sc-vs-first.b2: For something that is **impossible** or **not true now**, only the second conditional works: *If I **were** 20 years younger…* Not *If I am 20 years younger…*
sc-vs-first.w1: Don't mix: if + present, will (or if + past, would).
sc-modals.t: Could and might in the second conditional
sc-modals.s: Use **could** (= would be able to) or **might** (= perhaps would) in the result: *If I had time, I **could** help.* *If I could…* in the *if* clause = if I was able to.
sc-modals.b0: In the main clause, ***could*** means *would be able to*, and ***might*** means *perhaps would*: *If I had a car, I **could** drive you home.* *If you asked him nicely, he **might** say yes.*
sc-modals.b1: In the *if* clause, ***could*** means *was able to*: *If I **could** speak Japanese, I'd work in Tokyo.*
sc-modals.b2: Don't use *would* and *could* together for the same verb: *If I **could** swim, I'd go to the beach.* Not *If I would could swim…*
sc-modals.w0: Imaginary: could in the if clause.
sc-advice.t: Giving advice: If I were you…
sc-advice.s: **If I were you, I'd…** gives advice. *I'd…* alone, or *If I were in your position…*, also work.
sc-advice.b0: A very common way to give advice: ***If I were you**, I**'d** + base verb*: *If I were you, I'd talk to your manager.*
sc-advice.b1: Often the *if* clause is left out: *I**'d** see a doctor. I **wouldn't** worry about it.*
sc-advice.b2: More formal: *If I were in your position / in your shoes, I would…*
sc-advice.b3: In this phrase, ***were*** is the normal form, even in everyday English. *If I was you* is heard, but it's very informal. See [Was and Were](/blog/grammar/was-were/#ww-if-i-were).
sc-advice.w0: Advice: If I were you, I'd…
x.sc-form-use-s01: *If* + past simple for an imaginary situation.
q.sc-vs-first-s01: Which sentence is about an imaginary situation?
x.sc-vs-first-s01: *If I had wings* is impossible: second conditional.
x.sc-vs-first-s03: A real, likely situation: first conditional.
x.sc-advice-s02: Advice: *I would… if I were you*.
